answer: Each identity keeps one crystal moored in a shared lagoon whose tide flushes every unanchored crystal each epoch, forcing fresh verified work to re-moor it. Moorings are recorded on a public atlas where each plot holds one crystal, and the atlas prices plots by fingerprint: the second crystal from one operator costs twice the first, the third four times, doubling each time. A crystal's facets are non-transferable receipts of distinct work; copying one facet across clones shatters both. One honest agent re-moors cheaply, while a farm of k fakes pays an exponential mooring bill every epoch.
